answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making each new identity pass a memory-hard proof of work. The proof must hold a large RAM table that cannot be shared: a thousand parallel machines each still pay the full memory, so splitting one fortune into many accounts buys nothing. Every forged identity must rent real RAM, a cost that stays even as a river of clones floods the network; shared hardware drains a budget like a karst, leaving no ember of free influence. Peers verify the proof cheaply, trusting the hash is memory-bound. Cost is linear but non-shareable; a rich attacker can still buy nodes.
